evidence.exact_quote: Rule: stages 1–9 MUST be deterministic given the same inputs and filesystem state.

items.impact: Concurrent file, registry, permission, or account-state changes can produce different prompts while each implementation still claims the same inputs, and no reproducible oracle identifies the frozen filesystem state.
items.statement: The determinism rule does not define a snapshot boundary, content-hash set, or retry behavior for filesystem state that changes during stages 1 through 9.
items.title: Prompt determinism lacks a frozen filesystem boundary

evidence.exact_quote: - **Prompt pipeline carries tier identity.** `Prompt_Pipeline.md` §1.2 embeds tier/mode in the run envelope and instruction bundle. No node-identity, package-identity, or lane-identity fields exist.

items.impact: A reader or builder can implement retired tier identity despite the same canonical document already declaring node/package/lane/seam identity, fracturing runtime snapshots and cross-document consumers.
items.statement: The retained P5 material makes a present-tense assertion that node, package, and lane fields do not exist, directly conflicting with the canonical run-envelope fields earlier in the same document.
items.title: Retained P5 text contradicts current execution identity

evidence.exact_quote: - A safe preview of the compiled prompt (or its major sections) for transparency and debugging

items.impact: A transparency surface can expose secrets, private context, or hidden instructions, or can hide too much to support debugging, with no shared pass/fail oracle.
items.statement: The GUI requirement calls the compiled-prompt preview safe but does not define redaction classes, authorization, reveal controls, retention, copy/export policy, or accessible disclosure states.
items.title: Compiled-prompt preview safety is undefined

evidence.exact_quote: Prompt Pipeline is the canonical SSOT owner document for prompt pipeline behavior.
Prompt Pipeline owner-section requirements preserve product, runtime, storage, UI, and governance details in owner-section form.
Compatibility-only source vocabulary is noncanonical; live Prompt Pipeline wording uses the requested/effective owner terminology and the Puppet Master compliance baseline.

items.impact: These units establish document authority, preservation scope, and the noncanonical status of compatibility wording for downstream readers and validators.
items.statement: PP-002 through PP-004 consistently establish Prompt Pipeline ownership, owner-section preservation, and requested/effective terminology boundaries.
items.title: Document identity and terminology authority are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Prompt Pipeline owns prompt assembly stages, context compiler output incorporation, context compilation algorithms, compaction/pruning, rotation boundaries, and plugin prompt hook points, while other plans may consume outputs without redefining these algorithms.

Prompt assembly follows deterministic stages 1 through 9, applies mode-specific overlays during context compilation, applies plugin transforms and tool schemas, and carries the canonical orchestration flow contract for Orchestrator or delegated child runs.

Skill runtime delivery resolves requested skill refs from the PM registry, filters by permissions, de-duplicates by canonical skill id, bundles selected skill content when needed, and preserves on-demand access through the skill tool; provider-native skill directories are discovery/import/export/interoperability inputs only.

items.impact: The owner, input identity, stage ordering, and skill-delivery authority are sufficiently explicit to prevent alternate prompt compilers or provider-native skill stores from becoming peer runtime authorities.
items.statement: PP-005 through PP-009 define the SSOT boundary, reference map, execution identity, deterministic assembly order, overlay non-widening, and PM-native skill delivery path.
items.title: Assembly ownership and runtime delivery boundaries are coherent

evidence.exact_quote: Browser element attachments serialize after context compilation and before final conversation payload emission, preserving chip-based element context distinctions, bounded fields, truncation metadata, and DOM/page-body exclusion.

Browser selection attachments serialize after context compilation in stable thread-prep order before the user freeform message, preserving bounded browser selection fields and rejecting raw page bodies or blocked/expired chips.

items.impact: Implementations can choose incompatible text, HTML, URL, count, and lifetime limits and can surface blocked, expired, oversized, or unavailable browser state inconsistently.
items.statement: PP-010 and PP-011 require bounded browser attachments but define no numeric or model-derived bounds, URL disclosure policy, expiry clock, error taxonomy, or offline capture fallback oracle.
items.title: Browser attachment bounds and failure behavior are not falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: Document selection attachments serialize in stable order with bounded selection, routing, sensitivity, truncation, and revision payload metadata; structured revision providers use schema-enforced or locally validated revision shapes.

items.impact: A syntactically valid revision can still carry unsafe operations, stale anchors, conflicting edits, or partial application without a canonical abort, rollback, or user-confirmation result.
items.statement: The structured revision contract names shape and anchor validation but does not define operation_payload trust validation, conflict semantics, atomic application, partial-failure recovery, or destructive-change authorization.
items.title: Structured revisions lack transactional and trust semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Active Debug investigation context is normalized after context compilation and before final conversation serialization, with deterministic evidence ordering, source grouping identities, bounded summaries/refs, and explicit redaction/truncation state.

The compiled prompt includes an Instruction Bundle with active execution context, requested/effective overlay, Persona IDs, rules context, tool policy, Injected Context breakdown, and active Investigation Context summary when applicable.

Instruction Bundle rules keep Investigation Context additive, bound debug summaries, preserve revoked/blocked/expired/omitted visibility without serialization success, budget external instruction sources, treat PM-owned AGENTS.md as canonical, and keep provider-native instruction files as generated/import/export projections.

items.impact: The prompt path has one ordered normalization and authority chain for Debug evidence, execution identity, tool policy, and instruction-source projections.
items.statement: PP-013 through PP-015 consistently make Investigation Context additive, bounded, provenance-bearing, and subordinate to PM-owned instruction authority.
items.title: Investigation and instruction bundle authority is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: The compaction-immune set is partitioned into untouchable and truncatable tiers; only truncatable content is trimmed when over cap, and untouchable overflow emits diag.compaction_immune_overflow while execution continues.

items.impact: The runtime can be required to continue with a payload that the selected provider cannot accept, leaving abort, model switch, rotation, or degraded execution to incompatible builder choice.
items.statement: PP-016 and PP-017 preserve untouchable content and say execution continues when that content alone exceeds the cap, but they do not define how a provider-unfit payload can validly proceed or terminate.
items.title: Untouchable overflow has no executable terminal path

evidence.exact_quote: Context assembly preserves cache-friendly stable prefixes and applies explicit provider cache strategies for Anthropic, Google/Gemini, OpenAI, and unsupported surfaces without PM managing provider-owned cache state where not applicable.

items.impact: Concurrent refreshers, context mutation near expiry, logout or permission revocation, and network failure can reuse stale or over-disclosed cache resources without deterministic recovery or inspection state.
items.statement: The provider cache strategies do not specify cache-key composition, refresh locking, revocation and deletion, failed-refresh fallback, or stale-resource observability across accounts and permission snapshots.
items.title: Provider cache lifecycle and race handling are incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: Reasoning-block payloads are replay-safe state: PM preserves or converts them before compaction, maps provider-native reasoning_tokens into the UF-085 JSON-safe reasoning bucket / reasoning/thoughts display bucket with counting_semantics and no-double-count rules, tolerates out-of-order proxy delivery, and does not silently strip reasoning content due to adapter limitations.

Synthetic continue transitions through Idle, Eligible, ContinueInjected, ContinueObserved, and Suppressed, caps automatic attempts at 2, compares tail and prompt hashes, and emits diag.synthetic_continue_loop_prevented instead of retrying forever.

items.impact: Replay preserves causal state without double-counting usage, and automatic continuation is bounded by explicit states, hashes, diagnostics, and attempt limits.
items.statement: PP-019 through PP-022 define replay-safe reasoning, synthetic-content boundaries, continuation eligibility, and finite loop prevention as one coherent recovery path.
items.title: Replay and synthetic continuation have bounded state semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Dynamic context shrinking uses model-owned thresholds and emits low-context diagnostics when remaining context falls below 15 percent after tool output or injected context, with large tool-output markers using the 512 KiB policy boundary.

The agent-visible context-budget snapshot exposes effective window, used tokens/bytes, remaining percent, pressure state, previous compaction, tool-result shaping policy, deterministic budget allocation buckets, and priority classes.

items.impact: Different tokenizers, byte accounting, estimator timing, and model overrides can trigger different pressure states and truncation choices from the same assembled content.
items.statement: PP-023 and PP-024 mix percent, token, byte, and 512 KiB thresholds without naming the authoritative tokenizer, rounding, snapshot instant, or conformance fixtures for pressure calculations.
items.title: Context-pressure calculations lack a common measurement oracle

evidence.exact_quote: After filtering, pruning, or compaction, PM validates role alternation and message boundaries, prevents plugin transforms from deleting or reordering protected content, and either repairs malformed history with audited structural placeholders or aborts serialization.

items.impact: Support and replay consumers cannot reliably distinguish original content from a repair or prove which transform caused malformed history.
items.statement: PP-025 requires audited structural placeholders but does not define the audit record identity, causal transform ref, placeholder marker shape, persistence, or idempotent replay behavior.
items.title: Warn-and-repair placeholders lack an audit record contract

evidence.exact_quote: Rotation terminates a run and spawns a follow-up only after deterministic compaction/pruning fails against the final assembled payload; ask and plan are rotation-ineligible, regular and yolo are eligible, and rotated runs inherit continuity state and finish with done.rotated.

items.impact: A crash or retry between parent termination, child creation, and done.rotated persistence can lose the continuation or create duplicate follow-up runs.
items.statement: PP-026 defines rotation eligibility and inherited state but not atomic parent-child handoff, deduplication keys, crash recovery, or the ordering of child creation versus parent terminal persistence.
items.title: Rotation handoff is not atomic or retry-safe

evidence.exact_quote: The GUI exposes an Injected Context breakdown per run or turn, including paths, byte counts, truncation reason, and a safe preview of compiled prompt sections for transparency and debugging.

items.impact: The UI can misrepresent omitted versus redacted context, leak sensitive paths or prompt material, and provide inaccessible or unlocalizable diagnostic detail.
items.statement: PP-027 does not define redacted, omitted, unavailable, stale, or permission-denied GUI states, nor keyboard, screen-reader, localization, reveal, copy, or export behavior for sensitive context details.
items.title: Injected Context GUI lacks disclosure and accessibility states

evidence.exact_quote: Prompt assembly must follow the canonical stage ordering, and compaction must preserve protected tool outputs so skill outputs are not pruned.

items.impact: A build can pass the named acceptance gates while violating attachment safety, identity resolution, cache isolation, replay, GUI disclosure, rotation, recovery, accessibility, or failure behavior.
items.statement: PP-028 reduces document-level acceptance to stage ordering and skill-output preservation despite the document specifying many other safety-critical and user-visible behaviors.
items.title: Prompt Pipeline acceptance gates cover only a small fraction of canon

evidence.exact_quote: The requested/effective runtime pipeline is locked for provider family selection, account or server-profile resolution, billing or entity attribution, and PM-native skills/MCP assembly before provider handoff.

Before final prompt payload emission, runtime resolution follows the ordered surface, provider, account/profile, entitlement, effective runtime, skill readiness, MCP/tool availability, instruction bundle, and frozen snapshot stages, with PM-native skill/tool readiness derived from explicit dependency metadata and transported through normal prompt/context assembly.

items.impact: Provider, account/profile, entitlement, skills, MCP/tools, instruction assembly, and frozen handoff share an ordered pre-prompt authority path.
items.statement: PP-029 and PP-030 coherently establish the requested/effective runtime boundary and the ordered resolver-to-provider handoff.
items.title: Pre-prompt runtime resolution has a single ordered path

evidence.exact_quote: Prompt Pipeline preserves persona_selection_source as the canonical requested-Persona source enum and adds runtime_selection_source plus a human-readable selection_reason for inspectors and audit history.

Requested Persona precedence remains explicit override, scoped natural-language override, surface mapping, surface auto resolver candidate, config default, then canonical fallback; runtime/provider selection happens afterward and cannot rewrite the winning requested-Persona source.

Provider/runtime resolution preserves requested_platform, effective_platform, provider_family_id, effective account rows, effective connection_profile_id, and billing/entity bucket semantics while keeping provider examples distinct by runtime surface and auth family.

items.impact: Inspectors and recovery consumers may show different reasons or fallback behavior, and a no-eligible-runtime condition has no stable machine-readable transition or remediation contract.
items.statement: PP-031 through PP-033 define source labels, precedence, and effective identities but not a canonical reason-code enum, blocked/degraded state, retry rule, or recovery transition when no account, profile, entitlement, provider, or model is eligible.
items.title: Runtime resolution lacks machine-readable blocked and recovery states

segments.summary: Reviewed the complete assembly, attachment, compaction, cache, replay, continuation, context-pressure, integrity, and rotation prologue; identified the missing frozen-filesystem determinism boundary.

Reviewed GUI and acceptance text, the full effective-runtime continuation, retained P5 material, owner map, and PP-002 through PP-004; found a critical stale identity contradiction and an undefined safe-preview boundary while confirming SSOT identity units.
Reviewed PP-005 through PP-011 and all paired semantic units; confirmed assembly and skill authority while identifying non-falsifiable browser attachment bounds and failure behavior.
Reviewed PP-012 through PP-018 and all paired semantic units; confirmed investigation and instruction authority, and found structured-revision, unfit-overflow, and provider-cache lifecycle gaps.
Reviewed PP-019 through PP-025 and all paired semantic units; confirmed bounded replay and continuation states while finding missing measurement and placeholder-audit oracles.

Reviewed PP-026 through PP-033 and all paired semantic units; confirmed ordered pre-prompt resolution and identified rotation atomicity, GUI disclosure, acceptance coverage, and blocked-resolution gaps.
